best_for: Developers and DBAs who manage PostgreSQL databases and want a free graphical tool for queries, schema changes and backups, on the desktop or shared through a web server.
description:
pgAdmin 4 is the graphical management tool for PostgreSQL, built by the pgAdmin Development Team. Dave Page started the project nearly 30 years ago and still works on it, and the community translates it into other languages.

You can create, browse and change every kind of database object through forms, and pgAdmin shows you the SQL it generates, so nothing happens out of sight. The query tool has syntax highlighting, auto-completion and a query history. A graphical EXPLAIN shows where a slow query spends its time. Backup and restore dialogs save a database to a file and load it back, and you can sign in to pgAdmin with Kerberos or a GitHub account.

points.title: Desktop app or shared web server
points.text: pgAdmin runs as a desktop app for one person, or in server mode on a web server for a whole team. The Windows and Mac installers include both modes.

points.title: Free under the PostgreSQL license
points.text: pgAdmin is open source under the PostgreSQL license, with no paid edition. It also works with PostgreSQL-based databases such as EDB Advanced Server.

points.title: New version about every six weeks
points.text: The project ships a release roughly every six weeks. The Windows listing keeps 26 versions if an update breaks something for you.

points.title: A master password guards saved logins
points.text: Saved database passwords are encrypted with a master password you set. You can turn it off only by editing a config file, which the project advises against.

points.title: It is a web app in a window
points.text: Because pgAdmin is a web application, file open and save dialogs are its own, not your system's. That can feel odd next to native desktop apps.

points.title: Windows 10 and recent macOS
points.text: Version 7.0 and later need 64-bit Windows 10 or Server 2016 and newer; the installer comes in per-user and all-users forms. Version 9.19 supports macOS 14 Sonoma through 26 Tahoe on Intel and Apple Silicon.

points.title: Linux comes from the project's repo
points.text: This site lists Windows and macOS. On Linux you add the project's APT or RPM repository, use the dpage/pgadmin4 container, or install with pip. macOS lists only the current release here.
